nodes.v: The Invitation
If you can't call right now
Tell us what's happening and we'll ring you back as soon as the office opens. If you are in severe pain, please call rather than wait for us.

         What counts as a dental emergency?
        </button>

nodes.v: Severe or persistent pain, a knocked-out or fractured tooth, swelling that suggests infection, a lost filling or crown, uncontrolled bleeding from the mouth, or a denture that has broken and left you unable to eat. If you are unsure, call — that is what the phone is for.

nodes.v: Whenever possible, yes — the practice makes space in the schedule for emergencies. It cannot be guaranteed for every case on every day, and we would rather say that plainly than promise a slot that isn't there.

        </button>

nodes.v: No. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Outside those hours, leave a message using the form and we will call you back when we open. For anything involving severe trauma, uncontrolled bleeding or dizziness, call 911 rather than waiting.

        </button>

nodes.v: Pick it up by the crown, not the root. Keep it moist — in milk, or in your own saliva. Do not scrub it. Then call immediately, because this is the one dental emergency where the clock genuinely matters.

        </button>
